# Delays are not observed directly

## A delay is the time between two events

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Infection to symptom onset, onset to hospitalisation, onset to death
- Nowcasts, forecasts and transmission models take a delay
  distribution as given
- Neither event is seen at a point. Both arrive as a day, sometimes a
  week
- In real time the longer delays have not happened yet

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi], Lorentz Center, June 2026
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-double-censoring.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A timeline. A blue box marks the primary event window of
width w_P, a red box marks the secondary event window of width w_S, an
arrow between them is the delay T = S - P, and a dashed line further
right marks the observation cutoff C, beyond which longer delays have
not yet been seen."}
:::
::::

[hsi]: https://samabbott.co.uk/how-to-serial-interval

## Which adjustment a dataset needs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Interval censoring of both events applies to almost any line list
- Right truncation is the correction when the observation cutoff sits
  near the primary events
- How cases were ascertained matters. On the primary event the delay
  is right censored instead

::: {.attribution}
Fig 3 of
[Charniga et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012520),
PLOS Comput Biol, CC-BY 4.0
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-charniga-flowchart.png){height="800px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="A decision tree. Questions about time variation, whether the
analysis is retrospective or real time, whether the cutoff was near
the primary events, and which event cases were ascertained through,
lead to actions: adjust for interval censoring and right censoring,
adjust for interval censoring and right truncation, or interval
censoring alone."}
:::
::::

## 1. The primary event sits in a window

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The primary event falls somewhere in a window $[0, w_P]$
- It need not be uniform, but a uniform primary is fair when the
  window is short
- Mix the delay over where in the window the event sat, a convolution
  on the CDF
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-primary-censoring.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A timeline. The primary event sits at an unknown point tau
inside a blue window of width w_P, the secondary event is a single red
line, and the delay is f(t - tau) averaged over tau."}

$$
F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(t) = \int_{0}^{w_P} g(\tau)\, F(t - \tau)\, d\tau
$$

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi] · maths after
[primarycensored](https://primarycensored.epinowcast.org/)
:::
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
Gamma, lognormal and Weibull against a uniform primary have closed
forms.
:::

## 2. So does the secondary event

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The secondary event is recorded to the day as well
- The probability of a daily bin is a difference of the
  primary-censored CDF
- It doubles as the probability mass function for daily discrete-time
  models
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-secondary-censoring.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The primary-censored delay density, with the daily bin from n
to n + w_S shaded red and labelled as the difference of the CDF at its
two edges."}

$$
\Pr\!\big(T \in [n, n + w_S]\big)
  = F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n + w_S) - F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n)
$$

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi]
:::
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
In the past this was often written as a double integral, which is
typically more complicated to evaluate.
:::

## 3. In real time you only see the pairs that finished

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A pair enters the data only if the secondary event happened before
  the cutoff $C$
- Condition on being observed, so divide by the CDF at the horizon
- Short delays are over-represented early in an epidemic
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-truncation.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Five delays from one primary event. The three that end before
the cutoff C are drawn in red and observed, the two that end after it
are dashed and never seen, and the likelihood is divided by the CDF at
C minus P."}

$$
L^{\mathrm{RT}}
  = \frac{F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n + w_S) - F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n)}
         {F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(C - P)}
$$

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi]
:::
:::
::::
